stem: Which of the following does NOT belong to the same professional category as the other three? Accountant, Auditor, Surgeon, Cashier

per_option_rationale.rationale: An accountant is a finance professional whose work centres on financial records - part of the finance/accounts domain.
An auditor is a finance/assurance professional who examines financial accounts - part of the finance/accounts domain.
Accountant, Auditor, and Cashier all work within the finance and accounts domain. A surgeon is a medical professional operating in the healthcare domain, making it the odd one out.

A cashier handles financial transactions - part of the finance/accounts domain. A student might flag cashier as a lower-level role compared to accountant and auditor, but the property tested is professional domain, not seniority.

explanation: Accountant, Auditor, and Cashier are all finance/accounts professionals. Surgeon is a medical professional in the healthcare domain - a completely different field - and is therefore the odd one out.

explanation_sections.punchline: Three roles share the finance and accounts domain; the fourth belongs to a different professional field entirely.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: classify each role by professional domain. Setup decision: choose domain as the grouping criterion over seniority or qualification level. Accountant->finance, Auditor->finance, Cashier->finance, Surgeon->healthcare.
explanation_sections.lesson: When classifying roles as odd-one-out, professional domain (the field of work) is usually the correct grouping criterion, not seniority or qualification.
explanation_sections.timing: 45-55 seconds. The trap is mistaking Cashier as the odd one due to perceived seniority difference from Accountant and Auditor.
